question: Are findings F1–F4 resolved sufficiently to approve PR #790's credential security boundary?

tests: secret-bearing resolver/callback exceptions are replaced with stable non-secret codes
DPAPI child receives only allowlisted environment metadata, never ambient credentials
callback cannot return the raw credential in result/evidence
MCP internal errors never reflect store exception text
findings.proof: DPAPI subprocess environment is allowlisted; stdout/stderr buffers are cleared; decrypt and callback exceptions become fixed codes; callback results are recursively secret-scanned; MCP store failures become internal_error.

tests: binding mismatch and duplicate invocation refuse before credential/provider
findings.proof: All fields are inside the canonical SHA-256 digest; pointer resolution rechecks ID/location/hash/source/work hash and expiry; invocation binding plus durable invocationId reservation blocks substitution and replay.

tests: every executable credential/provider occurrence is explicitly classified; none is UNSAFE/BYPASS
audit implementation is AUDIT_TOOLING only while it has no executable credential/provider behavior
unknown executable credential-use path remains fail-closed UNSAFE/BYPASS
known broker/runtime paths retain explicit classification
governed EOS transport delegates credential resolution only to broker.withCredential
findings.proof: The governed EOS paid transport contains no process.env, API-key name, or Authorization-header construction and reaches the key only through broker.withCredential. Audit tooling is accepted only when an independent executable-behavior scan passes; otherwise it fails closed. Manual Owner-activated review tools remain isolated from the MCP/EOS broker runtime.

tests: per-invocation estimate above the authorized ceiling never resolves a credential
cumulative ceiling survives calls/retries and refuses before provider
durable ledger preserves cumulative spend and at-most-once ids across transport restart
provider pilot total/per-review guards remain green in full orchestration suite
findings.proof: Conservative per-call estimate is checked and durably reserved against the authorization's cumulative ceiling before credential/provider use; duplicate IDs and post-restart retries refuse; the independent outer provider guard retains $0.25 per-review and $10 aggregate pilot ceilings.

tokenFinding.reason: The first FACT_BASED run honestly attributed 7,268 estimated request tokens, but the generic security profile included up to 2,400 characters from each of twelve patches, producing 25,829 raw-source bytes. Provider measurement was 7,832 input tokens. The feed was fact-based but unnecessarily broad for a delta.
tokenFinding.correction: security-credential-boundary-delta sends only this compact resolution artifact, prior/content hashes, exact-head provenance, and the single F1–F4 question; it neither deletes necessary evidence nor resends original patches.
